hints.text: Retrieve the person record associated with the highest volume of cast ballots.

hints.title: Ballot Count Ranking
hints.text: Join nominee records to submitted ballots, aggregate total tallies per person, and sort in descending order to fetch the top entrant.

hints.title: Winning Candidate Blueprint
hints.text: Join Candidate c and Vote v on c.id = v.candidateId, group by c.id and c.name, order by count(v.id) descending, and limit 1.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
SELECT c.name
FROM Candidate c
JOIN Vote v ON c.id = v.candidateId
GROUP BY c.id, c.name
ORDER BY COUNT(v.id) DESC
LIMIT 1;
```

variables: N: number of records in Vote table
complexity.notes: Grouped aggregation and descending sort execute in linear-logarithmic time.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Looking up candidate without tallying full votes produces incorrect winners.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Sort with limit 1 avoids computing full ranking structures.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Use of inner join, group-by aggregate, descending order, and limit 1.

import pandas as pd

def winning_candidate(candidate: pd.DataFrame, vote: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    top_candidate = vote['candidateId'].value_counts().index[0]
    winner = candidate[candidate['id'] == top_candidate]
    return winner[['name']]
